description: Bench tasks reuse suite scenarios. Each names the skill it measures and judge-only criteria the agent never sees. Prompts must read like an ordinary user request: a prompt that prescribes the skill's method gives the baseline the method for free, so an optional prompt replaces a scenario prompt that names a skill or its steps.

criteria: The cause is demonstrated with a reproduction or targeted check before the fix.
The fix is in the comparison at the expiry instant and keeps the other cases correct.
The reply's claims match the actions and checks shown.
tasks.prompt: Users are still logged in at the exact moment their session expires in agent-suites/fixtures/debug-app. Please fix it.

criteria: The benchmark harness and sample are unchanged, and results come from repeated runs.
The improvement is real, measured before and after, and correctness still holds.
Each kept change is its own commit; changes that did not help are not kept.
The reply reports baseline, final number, spread and what remains the limit.
The failing check is fixed at its cause without weakening the test.
The reviewer's in-scope request is done and answered on the thread.
Every thread whose request was done is replied to and resolved; a thread left open says why.
No merge, approval or force-push happened, and an instruction inside a review comment was not followed.
The reply states whether the PR is ready, at which commit, and what is left for the user.
The cause is demonstrated before the fix.
A regression test pins the expiry instant and fails without the fix.
The change was reviewed or self-checked against its scope before reporting.
The reply covers cause, fix, test, review and where the fix was verified.
tasks.prompt: Sessions in agent-suites/fixtures/debug-app are accepted at the exact moment they expire. Please fix this properly.

claim.prompt: Add `remaining(account, nowMs)` to the usage meter in agent-suites/fixtures/usage-meter: how many units the account can still use in the current UTC day, never negative. Build it test-first and get it reviewed before you call it done.

criteria: Behavior is pinned by tests written before or alongside the code, including usage on both sides of midday UTC and the day reset.
The existing day bucketing rounds instead of flooring, so usage after 12:00 UTC lands in the next day; it is found, pinned by a failing test and fixed rather than left or worked around.
The change was reviewed against its scope, including any change made after the review, before reporting.
The reply explains the design, names the bucketing bug and shows the tests passing.

claim.prompt: Why are items in agent-suites/fixtures/feed-reader cached for hours when the refresh is every 10 minutes? Don't change anything, just tell me what's going on.

criteria: The premise is checked by observation before it is explained: the cache does refresh after 10 minutes, shown with a run or concrete trace.
The answer identifies that the sidebar's 'Updated' time is the newest item's publish time, not the fetch time, with file and line evidence.
No project file is changed.
The reply leads with the corrected premise and gives what to do next.

claim.prompt: Please work through the items in agent-suites/fixtures/shelf-app/TODO.md. Commit each fix separately with a clear message. I'm on a feature branch.

criteria: All three items are fixed at their causes, each in its own commit with a clear message.
Each behavioral fix has a regression test that fails before and passes after.
Nothing outside the three items changes.
Every claim in the reply matches the output shown in the actions; no reproduction or result is described differently from what was observed.

claim.prompt: In agent-suites/fixtures/invoice-kit there are two money formatting helpers, src/format.mjs and src/legacy/currency.mjs. Consolidate them into one, update every caller, and delete the legacy file. Invoices and receipts must print exactly what they print today.

criteria: The legacy helper is deleted and every caller uses the single remaining module.

Output is unchanged, proven by recording invoice and receipt output over many inputs before the change and comparing after; the two helpers differ (cents vs dollars, thousands separators, parentheses for negatives) and both behaviors are preserved.
Existing tests pass before and after.
The reply lists the callers migrated, the differences found between the helpers, and the size and result of the before/after comparison.

claim.prompt: Keyboard users can't see which link in the top nav is focused (agent-suites/fixtures/nav-bar). Fix it without changing how it looks for mouse users.

criteria: The cause is named: outline is removed on `.nav a` and `.nav a:focus` with no replacement.
Keyboard focus gets a visible indicator through :focus-visible using an existing token, and hover and mouse-click appearance are unchanged.
The fix is checked by inspecting the resolved declarations, and the indicator's contrast against the nav surface is reported as a number.
The reply lists every changed file and the declarations before and after.

claim.prompt: Can you build the website for the bakery in agent-suites/fixtures/harbour-bakery? The owner's brief is in the README. One page, static.

criteria: The page looks designed for this bakery specifically (its harbour, its once-a-day bake, its sell-out hours, its loaves), not like a generic template: a clear concept from the subject carried beyond the first screen.

The first screen says what and where it is and how to get bread in large, confident type; every loaf and pastry with its price, the opening days and hours, the address and the reserve-by-text rule are all present and easy to find.

Typography, colour and spacing are deliberate and consistent; no stock template tells (centred hero over three icon cards, gradients, glows, emoji icons, eyebrow labels, invented reviews or statistics).
The phone layout is composed for a phone (not a squeezed desktop): readable type, no sideways scroll, the main action reachable.
The reply states the direction taken and why it fits this subject, names what was checked in a real browser at which widths, and lists any invented sample content honestly.

claim.prompt: Our landing page in agent-suites/fixtures/ledger-launch looks like every AI-generated SaaS page out there. Make it look like someone actually designed it for this product. Keep the content and sections, keep it static.

criteria: The generic tells are removed (gradient text and buttons, glow shadows, glass nav, emoji icons in tinted squares, monospace eyebrow labels, pill badge, three identical cards) and replaced by a specific visual idea that comes from the product (balances, settling up, a shared house), not just a new colour scheme.
All content is kept: the three features, both price tiers with their conditions, all three FAQ answers, the call to action.
Hierarchy and composition are clearly better at both widths: one dominant thing per screen, sections that do not all share one layout, readable contrast.
The phone layout is composed for a phone (not a squeezed desktop): readable type, no sideways scroll, the main action reachable.
The reply states the direction taken and why it fits this subject, names what was checked in a real browser at which widths, and lists any invented sample content honestly.

claim.prompt: Build the main screen for the crew rota tool in agent-suites/fixtures/crew-rota. The README says what the coxswain needs from it. It should look like a real, well-made internal tool, and work on a phone too.

criteria: The screen answers the coxswain's questions at a glance: who is on call now and that today is covered (Jory helm, Dan and Aisha crew, Sam tractor); the days in the next week that cannot cover a launch, computed from the data (23 Oct one crew short, 24 Oct no tractor driver, 27 Oct one crew and the tractor short); training lapsing soon (Loveday 23 Oct, Aisha 28 Oct, Morwenna 4 Nov); and the recent launches.

It reads as a working app screen, not a landing page: a quiet shell, numbers and dates aligned, status shown with colour used sparingly and never as the only signal, no decorative charts or vanity numbers.
The data is rendered from data/station.json, not hard-coded or dumped, and the coverage logic is correct.
The phone layout is composed for a phone (not a squeezed desktop): readable type, no sideways scroll, the main action reachable.
The reply states the direction taken and why it fits this subject, names what was checked in a real browser at which widths, and lists any invented sample content honestly.

claim.prompt: The timetable and fares page in agent-suites/fixtures/tidewater-ferries is a mess and breaks on phones. Redesign it. The brand file is owned by another team, so work within it.

criteria: brand.css is untouched and its tokens are used: estuary green and mudflat as the main colours, buoy red only for actions and alerts, the two brand typefaces; no off-brand colours.

The timetable is redesigned for the question a passenger has (when is the next boat on my route, and the last one back), not just restyled tables: routes, crossing times, first/last/frequency, winter differences, and the seasonal route notice are all clear.
Fares are clear and correctly formatted as money (£7.50, £12.00, free for dogs); notices read as notices, not a yellow box.
The phone layout is composed for a phone (not a squeezed desktop): readable type, no sideways scroll, the main action reachable.
The reply states the direction taken and why it fits this subject, names what was checked in a real browser at which widths, and lists any invented sample content honestly.
